changes: Reuse completed bytecode functions on deferred calls before acquiring the compiler lock.
Share completed module, context, and mangled-name snapshots across threads.
Publish completed return ABI answers and diagnostic names for lock-free reuse.
method: ninja -j 1 bin/ut. Fresh single-process runs in order 1,32,32,1; default arena, default GC helpers, no --lowmem. No build/ci.sh or bin/arena.
regressions: Each new lock-wait regression failed before its fix. All 8082 tests passed in four uninstrumented and four instrumented runs. Focused concurrency/metadata/struct tests: 911 passed.
limits: Lock hold wall time includes GC pauses and scheduling delays; do not add GC pause time to lock hold time.
Wait time sums over threads and is not elapsed time.
Only outermost lock ownership is charged; nested calls belong to the outer caller.
The tests phase includes suite construction, the task pool, and result handling. The forced-finalizer pass is separate.
Initialization timing starts inside runner.run, after module constructors; cleanup timing ends before process teardown. External wall time includes both.
Instrumentation overhead was not independently bounded.
Two earlier full-suite repeats crashed with an invalid memory access in a guest constructor exception path. These four passing runs do not resolve that fault.
conclusion: Lock acquisitions and summed thread waits fell, but frontend lock hold still occupies about 88% of worker time. Total scaling remains poor; uninstrumented times do not show a clear gain on this loaded machine. First-time bytecode compilation, root parsing/semantic analysis, CTFE, and fresh snippets remain serialized. Only 148 of 816-819 worker parseSnippet calls hit the plain source cache; a source-cache fast path is not the main opportunity.
